schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: WITH HEL AS ( SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS INSTALL_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) SELECT C.INSTALL_DATE AS INSTALL_DT , INSTALLS, ROUND(IFNULL(REN,0)/INSTALLS,2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM( SELECT INSTALL_DATE, COUNT(PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS FROM HEL GROUP BY INSTALL_DATE) C LEFT JOIN (SELECT A.INSTALL_DATE,COUNT(B.EVENT_DATE) AS REN FROM HEL A JOIN ACTIVITY B ON A.PLAYER_ID=B.PLAYER_ID AND A.INSTALL_DATE-B.EVENT_DATE=-1 GROUP BY A.INSTALL_DATE) D ON C.INSTALL_DATE=D.INSTALL_DATE

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they handle the calculation of DAY1_RETENTION differently. Q1 calculates the retention rate by dividing the count of players who made an event on the day after their first login by the total number of players. Q2, on the other hand, calculates the retention rate by dividing the count of players who made an event on the day after their first login by the total number of players, but it uses a LEFT JOIN which can lead to different results if there are players without events on the day after their first login.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in results can be observed when there are players who do not have events on the day after their first login. In this case, Q1 will not count these players in the denominator, while Q2 will.
